Ophthalmology Clinic - Retina Consult

Patient: 58-year-old with longstanding type 2 diabetes mellitus, presenting for follow-up of diabetic eye disease.

Subjective: Patient reports gradually worsening blurry vision in the right eye over the past several months, denies acute floaters or flashes today. No prior laser treatment.

Assessment: Diabetic retinopathy, high risk proliferative changes noted on prior visits with neovascularization of the disc. Given the elevated risk of vision loss from progression to vitreous hemorrhage or tractional retinal detachment, decision made to proceed with treatment now rather than continue observation, as the risk of continued watching outweighs the risks associated with laser treatment.

Plan: Discussed panretinal photocoagulation with patient, risks and benefits reviewed including risk of decreased night vision and peripheral field constriction. Patient consents to proceed with laser treatment today.

Procedure: Panretinal (scatter) laser photocoagulation performed to the right eye by treating ophthalmologist under topical anesthesia, using standard scatter pattern sparing the macula. Approximately 1200 burns applied over one session. Patient tolerated procedure well without complication.

Follow up scheduled in 4 weeks to assess response and determine need for additional sessions.
